title: Home & everyday objects
goal: Name rooms and household objects, say where things are, and say what there is (and isn't) in a place.
intro:
Marathi doesn't have separate words for 'in', 'on', 'under' that sit before the noun like English prepositions. Instead they **attach to the end of the noun**: घर*ात* 'in the house', टेबल*ावर* 'on the table', पलंग*ाखाली* 'under the bed'.

This unit teaches the most common of these postpositions and how the noun changes shape (the **oblique** form) before them.

There's a lift near the stairs.

grammar.title: Postpositions as suffixes and the oblique form
grammar.body:
Location words attach to the end of the noun. Before them, many nouns change to an **oblique** form:

**m / n ending in a consonant:** add -आ-: घर → घरा**त** 'in the house', टेबल → टेबला**वर** 'on the table', पलंग → पलंगा**खाली** 'under the bed'
**m ending in -आ:** -आ → -या: पंखा → पंख्या**खाली**, जिना → जिन्या**जवळ**
**f ending in -ई:** no change: खोली → खोली**त**, खुर्ची → खुर्ची**वर**
**f ending in a consonant:** add -ई-: भिंत → भिंती**वर**, बॅग → बॅगे**त** (-ए- with some loans)

The main suffixes: **-त** in · **-वर** on · **-खाली** under · **-जवळ** near · **-मागे** behind · **-समोर** opposite · **-शेजारी** next to · **-मध्ये** in.

With pronouns, use the possessive oblique: माझ्या**जवळ** 'near me', तुमच्या**समोर** 'in front of you'.

examples.en: The book is in the cupboard.
The cat is under the bed.
The bottle is on the chair.
There's a photo on the wall.
The bank is opposite the school.
I don't have the key on me.

grammar.title: There is / there are
grammar.body:
'There is' is simply **place + thing + आहे**; 'there are' uses **आहेत**. The negative is **नाही / नाहीत**.

To ask whether something exists, add **का**: इथे बँक आहे का? 'Is there a bank here?'

**कोणी** = 'anyone / someone', **काही** = 'anything / something': घरात कोणी नाही 'there's no one home', फ्रिजमध्ये काही नाही 'there's nothing in the fridge'.

examples.en: There are two windows in the room.
Is there a shop near here?
There's no fan in the kitchen.

dialogue.title: Looking at a flat
dialogue.setting: Tanvi is viewing a flat to rent in Mumbai with a broker.

lines.speaker: Broker
lines.en: Come, come in. This is the living room.

lines.speaker: Tanvi
lines.en: Is there a wardrobe in the bedroom?

lines.speaker: Broker
lines.native: हो, भिंतीत मोठं कपाट आहे. आणि पलंग पण आहे.
lines.roman: ho, bhintīt moṭhaṃ kapāṭ āhe. āṇi palaṅg paṇ āhe.
lines.en: Yes, there's a big built-in wardrobe. And there's a bed too.

lines.speaker: Broker
lines.en: There's a fan in every room.

lines.speaker: Broker
lines.native: बेडरूमच्या शेजारी. आणि खिडकीतून समुद्र दिसतो!
lines.roman: beḍrūmchyā shedzārī. āṇi khiḍkītūn samudra disto!
lines.en: Next to the bedroom. And you can see the sea from the window!

culture: Shoes and sandals (चपला) come off at the door of every Marathi home — look for the pile outside. Many homes have a small shrine (देवघर) in the kitchen or a corner of the living room. In Mumbai, flats are described by size as 1BHK, 2BHK ('वन बीएचके'), and the building society (सोसायटी) and its watchman (वॉचमन) are part of daily life.

tip.title: There is, there are
tip.body:
- Place + thing + **आहे** = 'there is'; for more than one, **आहेत**: घरात तीन खोल्या आहेत.
- Negative: **नाही / नाहीत**. Ask with **का** at the end.
- 'In' is the ending **-त**: घरात, खोलीत, स्वयंपाकघरात.
- **कोणी** anyone, **काही** anything: घरात कोणी नाही.

sentences.en: There are three rooms in the house.
How many rooms are there in your house?
Is anyone in the kitchen?
There's no one in the living room.
There's no water in the bathroom.
Is there anything to eat in the kitchen?
Mum is in the kitchen.
Come in, sit down.
My room is really nice.

tip.title: On, under, in: endings on the noun
tip.body:
- 'On', 'under' and 'in' stick to the end of the noun: टेबला**वर** 'on the table', पलंगा**खाली** 'under the bed', कपाटा**त** 'in the cupboard'.
- A noun ending in a consonant adds **-आ-** first: टेबल → टेबलावर. One ending in -आ changes it to **-या-**: जिना → जिन्याखाली.
- Nouns in -ई don't change: खुर्चीवर, खोलीत.

sentences.en: My phone is on the bed.
The money is in the cupboard.
What's under the bed?
The phone isn't on the table.
The key's under the table!
My sister is upstairs.
Grandma is downstairs.

lessons.title: In the bag, near the book

tip.title: मध्ये, जवळ, मागे, समोर
tip.body:
- **मध्ये** 'in' is common with English words: बॅगमध्ये, फोनमध्ये.
- **जवळ** near · **मागे** behind · **समोर** opposite. They take the same -आ- form: पुस्तकाजवळ, घरामागे, घरासमोर.
- With 'my / your' use **माझ्या-**, **तुझ्या-**: तुझ्याजवळ किल्ली आहे का? 'Have you got the key on you?'

sentences.en: The water bottle is in the bag.
The book is in the bag.
The phone is next to the book.
Have you got the key on you?
There's a school opposite our house.
The children are behind the house.
There are two books in my bag.
There's no water in the bottle.

lessons.title: Doors, windows and the stairs

tip.title: Plural of -ई words
tip.body:
- Feminine nouns in **-ई** make the plural in **-या**: खिडकी → खिडक्या, खुर्ची → खुर्च्या, खोली → खोल्या.
- Feminine nouns ending in a consonant add **-ई**: भिंत → भिंती.
- **शेजारी** 'next to' takes **-च्या**: बाथरूमच्या शेजारी. As a noun it means 'neighbour'.

new: माझ्या खोलीत एक पलंग आणि दोन खुर्च्या आहेत.

sentences.en: There are three windows in the living room.
There are no chairs in the room.
Sit on the chair.
What's on the wall?
There's a cupboard under the stairs.
My room is next to the bathroom.
Please shut the door.
Our neighbours are really nice.

tip.title: Telling people what to do
tip.body:
- To a friend, a command is the bare verb: **लाव**, **कर**, **बस**. Politely add **-आ**: लावा, करा, बसा.
- पंखा / दिवा **लावणे** = switch on; **बंद करणे** = switch off.
- **ना** at the end softens it: पंखा लाव ना.
- **इथे** here · **तिथे** there · **बाहेर** outside.

sentences.en: Turn on the light, will you? (to a friend)
Please switch off the fan. (polite)
Shut the door, will you? (to a friend)
Please take your sandals off here. (polite)
Sit over there. (polite)
Come outside, please. (polite)
There's no fan here.
The key's over there, on the table.
The children are outside.
